'''Franck Barthe''' is a French mathematician.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~barthe/|title=Franck Barthe's Home Page|website=www.math.univ-toulouse.fr|access-date=2017-03-29}}</ref> He was awarded the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] (ECM) prize in 2004.<ref name=EMS2004>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.kth.se/4ecm/prizes.ecm.html|title=EMS Prize 2004|website=www.math.kth.se|accessdate=26 November 2017}}</ref> He is working as a professor of mathematics at [[Paul Sabatier University]].

== Work ==

Franck Barthe is known for his reverse form of the [[Brascamp-Lieb inequality]].<ref>{{citation|first=Franck|last=Barthe| title=On a reverse form of the Brascamp-Lieb inequality.  |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]|volume=134|year=1998|issue=2 |pages=335–361|doi=10.1007/s002220050267 |arxiv=math/9705210|bibcode=1998InMat.134..335B }}.</ref> With [[Keith Martin Ball|Keith M. Ball]], [[Shiri Artstein]], and [[Assaf Naor]], he solved Shannon's problem of the monotonic [[Entropy (information theory)|entropy]] increase of sums of [[random variable]]s.<ref>{{citation|first1= Shiri| last1= Artstein| first2=Franck|last2=Barthe|first3=Assaf| last3= Naor| title=Solution of Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy.  |journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=17|year=2004| issue= 4|pages=975–982| doi= 10.1090/S0894-0347-04-00459-X}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2004, he received the EMS Prize (prize presentation: [[Isoperimetric inequality|isoperimetric inequalities]], [[probability measure]]s and [[convex geometry]]) for his leading role in the application of mass-theoretical transport techniques.<ref name=EMS2004/>

In 2005, he received the [[Grand Prix Jacques Herbrand]].
